therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with active rheumatoid arthritis on background methotrexate plus a TNF inhibitor (etanercept or adalimumab)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Proportion of participants with at least one serious infection through Week 24

results.effect_size: Serious infection rate: rituximab 3% vs placebo 0%; ACR20 at Week 24: rituximab 30% vs placebo 17%
results.target_engagement_evidence: Lymphocyte assessments of T- and B-cell populations conducted; no clinically significant immunological findings reported
biomarker_changes: RF and anti-CCP antibody concentrations assessed
No clinically significant immunological or laboratory findings in either arm
subgroup_findings: Any infection through Week 24: rituximab arm 18 participants, placebo arm 11 participants
Any Grade 3/4 infection through Week 24: rituximab arm 3 participants, placebo arm 0 participants
Any AE through Week 24: rituximab arm 31 participants, placebo arm 15 participants
Any SAE through Week 24: rituximab arm 2 participants, placebo arm 0 participants
safety_signals: Serious infections occurred in 3% of rituximab-treated participants vs 0% placebo
Grade 3/4 infections in 3 rituximab participants vs 0 placebo participants
SAEs in 2 rituximab participants vs 0 placebo participants

Cumulative rituximab SAEs included arthritis infective (4/49), coronary artery occlusion (1/49), pneumonia (1/49), cellulitis (1/49), osteomyelitis (1/49), neutropenia (1/49), interstitial lung disease (1/49)
Trial terminated for business reasons unrelated to safety

context.comparator: placebo (on background methotrexate plus TNF inhibitor)
context.investigator_commentary: Sponsor decided to end long term extension phase for business reasons unrelated to safety.

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Methotrexate background therapy was hypothesized to support rituximab efficacy by preventing immunogenic responses and maintaining disease control
modulation_entries.citation: Participants must have been treated with MTX ≥15 mg per week and ≤25 mg per week for at least 12 weeks immediately prior to Day 1, at a stable dose for at least 4 weeks and was continued for the study duration.
